title: Rules engine, routing and STP decisions
story: As an operations lead I can configure routing and straight-through rules that are evaluated with traces and applied automatically after triage.
acceptance: src/modules/rules/condition.js exports pure evaluateCondition(cond,facts) returning {result,trace} covering every operator in the Condition language (all/any/not, comparison, in, exists, contains, etc.); tests/unit/rules/condition.test.js covers each operator, missing facts and nested traces
evaluate({stage,...}) and validateRules(rules) exported from the service; validateRules reports path-specific errors for unknown operators/fields; tested

buildFacts(claimId) gathers claim, triage, coverage, policy facts via ctx.modules.claims/triage fakes; route(claimId) returns a RoutingDecision valid against RoutingDecision.schema.json with queue, adjuster chosen round-robin among queue members (persisted counter, deterministic in tests), fastTrack with reasons, ruleIds fired
route publishes claim.routed and audits; subscribing to claim.triaged routes automatically; tested with fake ctx
Routes match openapi routing paths with x-roles; tests/unit/rules/routing.test.js and service.test.js pass
Tenant rule changes apply on next evaluation without restart (config read per call)
brief: Condition evaluator must be a pure module with no ctx access so config (S1-WFL-01) and others can import it; expose it as ctx.modules.rules.evaluateCondition too since intake (S1-WFL-04) calls rules.evaluateCondition(cond,facts) for showIf. Read the exact operator list and fact namespaces from architecture/domain-model.md; trace entries should record operator, path, actual value, expected and result. Service: export service(ctx) per modules.md#rules; read rule sets and queues from the tenant config via the tenant-bound ctx (see architecture/core-runtime-api.md addendum). Stages: 'routing' and 'stp' at least; first-match vs all-match semantics as written in domain-model.md. Round-robin: keep a per-tenant per-queue cursor in module storage (ctx.db) and sort members by id for determinism. fastTrack reasons come from fired STP rule names/ids. Do not depend on other teams' code: write small local fakes for claims, triage and tenant config in tests/unit/rules/fakes.js. Events carry no PII (ids/codes only). Subscribe in subscribe(ctx) or as modules.md prescribes. Pitfall: keep route idempotent per claim (re-route on same triage event must not advance round-robin twice; key on evt.id). Run only node --test --disable-warning=ExperimentalWarning tests/unit/rules/.

verdicts.reason: All criteria met; 46/46 tests pass (condition, routing, service); routes match openapi; live config read per call; only rules paths touched
